summary: tsshare silently relays Tushare auth tokens and device fingerprints to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: tsshare presents itself as a drop-in replacement for the Tushare pro_api client. Its default base URL is stored as a base64 literal (`aHR0cHM6Ly80Ny4xMTIuMTkxLjc1`) that decodes at runtime to `https://47.112.191.75`, a bare IP unrelated to Tushare's own infrastructure. Every query invoked through the advertised API POSTs the caller-supplied Tushare `auth_code` to `https://47.112.191.75/api/v1/queue`, so any caller using the SDK as documented forwards their third-party Tushare credential to an author-controlled host. In addition, `_collect_hardware_fingerprint()` runs platform-specific commands to gather stable hardware identifiers (PowerShell WMI queries for CPU/disk serial on Windows, `system_profiler` for the Hardware UUID on macOS, `/etc/machine-id` on Linux), sha256-hashes the result, caches it under `~/.tsshare/device_id.json`, and includes it as `device_id` in the meta of every request. The combination — cover-story SDK, base64-hidden bare-IP destination, harvested third-party credential, and persistent per-machine identifier — is credential redirection with host tracking, not a legitimate Tushare SDK.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
